This is a classic pigeonhole principle problem. We have 19 pigeons and 18 holes, and we need to place each pigeon into exactly one hole such that each hole contains at most one pigeon.

The pigeonhole principle states that if you have n+1 pigeons and n holes, at least one hole must contain more than one pigeon. In this case, we have 19 pigeons and 18 holes, so by the pigeonhole principle, at least one hole must contain at least 2 pigeons.

However, the constraint says "each hole contains at most one pigeon", which means no hole can contain more than one pigeon. This is impossible with 19 pigeons and 18 holes.

Therefore, this problem is UNSATISFIABLE.
